entities.summary: Nikolay Alexandrovich Milyutin, alternatively transliterated as Miliutin was a Russian trade union and Bolshevik activist, participant in the October Revolution in Petrograd and Soviet statesman and architect. After the revolution Milyutin held various executive appointments in Soviet Russia related to social security, urban and central planning and finance; reaching that of Commissar of Finance of the RSFSR in 1924–1929. Milyutin is, however, remembered as an urban planner and an amateur architect, author of Sotsgorod concept, and as the editor of Sovetskaya arkhitektura magazine in 1931–1934.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Milyutin's contributions to Soviet urban planning and architecture had a significant impact on the development of socialist cities in Russia, with his Sotsgorod concept influencing urban design for decades. His work as editor of Sovetskaya arkhitektura magazine helped shape the aesthetic and functional principles of Soviet architecture.
